Class HudCycleStrip

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.hud.HudCycleStrip
public final class HudCycleStrip extends Object
The cycle strip: a small hotbar drawn just right of the vanilla one, showing a ring of stacks that cycles through the held hotbar slot, with a spring slide each time the ring turns (since 7.1.0).

A mod that rotates stacks through a hotbar slot (a column of the inventory, a few extra slots behind the hotbar, anything with a ring) registers a HudCycleStrip.Source. Every frame the HUD draws, MenuKit asks each source for its HudCycleStrip.View of the selected hotbar slot and draws what comes back. The sources never draw, and the strip never knows which mod a ring belongs to, so one strip serves every mod.

Rows and columns

A source's HudCycleStrip.Source.axis() says which way its ring reads. A HudCycleStrip.Axis.ROW ring is a mini hotbar at the hotbar's height. A HudCycleStrip.Axis.COLUMN ring is one cell at the hotbar's height holding the held stack, with the rest of the ring rising above it. When a row and a column are both active on the selected slot they draw as a cross that shares the held cell, so the held stack is drawn once. At most one ring per axis draws: if two sources of the same axis are active on one slot, the one registered first wins.

The slide

The strip slides only when told to. After a source's ring turns, call slide(HudCycleStrip.Source, int, HudCycleStrip.Direction); the strip animates from where each stack was to where the view now puts it, over SLIDE_MILLIS on an ease-out-back spring. A ring that changes because something else moved the held stack (a mod that rotates whole hotbar rows, say) uses snapshot(int) before and slideChanged(int, HudCycleStrip.Direction, Map) after: only the rings whose contents actually changed slide, and only their held cell moves.

Usage: 

// client initializer
HudCycleStrip.Source source = hotbarSlot ->
        enabled() ? new HudCycleStrip.View(ringFor(hotbarSlot), 0) : null;
HudCycleStrip.register(source);

// later, right after the ring turned one step toward the hand
HudCycleStrip.slide(source, hotbarSlot, HudCycleStrip.Direction.FORWARD);

The guide is docs/cycle-strip.md.

    • register

      public static void register(HudCycleStrip.Source source)
      Registers a source. Registering the same instance twice does nothing.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - after MenuKit's declarations froze at client start

    • slide

      public static void slide(HudCycleStrip.Source source, int hotbarSlot, HudCycleStrip.Direction direction)
      Slides source's ring on hotbarSlot one step in direction. Call it right after the ring turned, once the source's view already shows the new order. A slide started while one is running starts over from the new order.

    • snapshot

      public static Map<HudCycleStrip.Source, @Nullable HudCycleStrip.View> snapshot(int hotbarSlot)
      Every registered source's view of hotbarSlot right now, for a later slideChanged(int, HudCycleStrip.Direction, Map). A source with no ring there maps to null, so a ring appearing or vanishing counts as a change.

    • slideChanged

      public static void slideChanged(int hotbarSlot, HudCycleStrip.Direction direction, Map<HudCycleStrip.Source, @Nullable HudCycleStrip.View> before)
      Slides the held cell of every ring on hotbarSlot whose contents differ from before (a snapshot(int) taken before the change). The rest of each strip stays still: this is for a change that moved the held stack, not the ring. A ring whose contents did not change does not move.
